title: Pending fragment
description: One captured entry waiting to land: the lane it claims, the instant the capture stated, and the entry itself. A fragment states a new entry, never a copy of anything a lane file holds. The entry mirrors the lane entry's field definitions so the fragment can be checked single-file; the lane file page owns the definitions, and keeping this mirror in agreement with the lane schema is a review responsibility. Closing fields are forbidden because a capture is never a close.

lane.description: The planning lane the entry wants to land in. A work lane is excluded: landing there would be a transition, and a transition owes a journal event.

captured.description: The instant the capture stated, RFC 3339 UTC with Z, second precision. The drain's ordering key; nothing reads a filesystem timestamp or repository history.

entry.description: The entry as it will appear in the lane file, minus everything only a close may add. Only id and type are required here, where the lane entry also requires points and summary: capture writes those two absent for the operator to fill, and the fragment is committed as captured, so a schema that required them would reject every capture at its own commit. The drain is what refuses an incomplete fragment, naming the file and the field.

id.description: The title's slug, plus at most a qualifying postfix where that slug was taken.

needs_id.description: A dependency target, restated from the lane entry: a bare id naming an entry in this record, or <alias>#<id> naming an entry in an attached peer. Keeping this mirror in agreement with the lane schema is the same review responsibility the entry object already carries.
